calibration.surprise_note: Validation against the real 2026-06-10 payloads reproduced every stall the audit had found manually: five failing builds and three never-persisted legacy dirs, with 28 fresh surfaces.

change_summary: Added quant/sleeve_health.py (build status from daily payloads + snapshots.jsonl staleness in US equity sessions, one JSONL health row per day) and wired it into quant/run.py after the sleeve payload assembly with warning logs for failing or stalled sleeves.
hypothesis: Sleeve builders that early-return empty snapshots persist nothing and write no skip record, so dead accumulation surfaces are invisible; a central daily sleeve-health report that records every sleeve build status and on-disk snapshot staleness makes stalls visible within one day.
next_retry_requires: per-sleeve cadence overrides if false positives appear
notes: Verified by re-runnable checks in this runner (real-payload validation catches the known stalls) plus the full quant pytest suite (1308 passed, including 4 new tests).

post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not silence or threshold-away health warnings instead of fixing the underlying sleeve; do not move health reporting into individual builders where new sleeves can forget it.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: If a sleeve legitimately emits less than weekly, add a per-sleeve expected-cadence override instead of raising the global threshold.
post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: Three independent silent stalls shared one pattern: early-return without persistence. Rather than patching every builder, a central read-side report over the payloads the run already assembles plus on-disk freshness covers current and future sleeves uniformly.

prediction.confidence_reason: The audit traced three independent silent stalls to the same pattern of early-return-without-persistence; a read-side central report over the daily snapshot payloads plus on-disk snapshots.jsonl freshness needs no change to any sleeve builder, so trading-day behavior is untouched and the main risks are key-name drift in run.py payloads and false stale flags for sleeves that legitimately emit rarely, both handled by session-based thresholds and explicit never-persisted status.

production_impact.parity_note: Read-side observability only: scans already-built daily payloads and snapshot files, appends a health row, and logs warnings. No sleeve builder, order, or replay path changed.
